$comment: Accepted MISSING findings for tools/osm-drift-check.py, keyed by IDENTITY (slug|reason), never by count — a count ratchet stays green when one entry is resolved and another vanishes the same week, which is the event this check exists to catch. Adding a key here is a DECISION: write a note saying why. Removing a facility from the site is a separate, later act.
$adjudication_2026_08_19: The eight entries this file shipped with on 2026-08-19 were adjudicated one at a time under TODO #1228, each against the OSM object's own version history (api.openstreetmap.org/api/0.6/<type>/<id>/history.json), the changeset that made the edit, an Overpass re-query of the surrounding area, and a named second source. NOT ONE of the eight was a closure. Seven were MERGES — a POI node deleted and its tags moved onto the building polygon at the same spot, which is routine OSM housekeeping and looks identical, from an id lookup, to a facility that shut down. One (Elliot Provincial Hospital) was a RETAG of the wrong polygon: in changeset 185535921 the mapper correctly re-identified way:217484563 as Elliot High Hostel on Barry Way and moved the hospital's own tags onto way:461683581 at 1 Maclear Road, so OUR id was wrong and always had been. All eight facility_ids were repointed at the surviving object and their coordinates re-read from it; two of ours were badly wrong (H.A. Grove by 1.3 km, Elliot Provincial by 1.9 km), which on this site is a trip someone cannot afford. Zero records were deleted and no URL changed. The lesson worth keeping: a deleted OSM node is a question, not an answer — six of the seven merges were made by one experienced South African mapper (VisibleSouth, ~6,400 changesets) whose changeset comments name the facility being tidied.
$reconciliation_2026_08_21: THREE NUMBERS, ONE QUESTION, NO CONTRADICTION (#1351/#1363, reconciled 2026-08-21). The clinicfinder keeper reported '4 published facilities no longer exist in OpenStreetMap' (2026-08-19 21:15 SAST), this check reported MISSING 1, and a full Overpass sweep the next day reported 0. All three were true answers, and the disagreement is a TIMELINE plus a MISLABELLED COUNT, not a data defect. (1) THE KEEPER'S 4 WAS CORRECT AND IS NOW STALE. It queried the 517 records then claiming services.emergency_24h using their PRE-#1228 facility_ids. The set of records #1228 repointed INTERSECTED WITH emergency_24h is EXACTLY 4, by name: ha-grove-hospital-mpumalanga (zaf_node_1460687699), tower-psychiatric-hospital-eastern-cape (zaf_node_7896380488), general-justice-gizenga-mpanza-regional-hospital-formerly-stanger-hospital-durba (zaf_node_9048293718) and elliot-provincial-hospital-eastern-cape (zaf_way_217484563). The repoints landed in commit a431ac6 at 22:17 SAST — 62 minutes after the keeper measured them, and eight hours before /site-review-headless filed #1351 from the already-superseded capture at 06:30 the next morning. Nothing was ever left broken. (2) NOT ONE OF THE 4 HAD CLOSED, verified against the OSM API on 2026-08-21. node/1460687699, node/7896380488 and node/9048293718 all answer HTTP 410 GONE: each was a POI node deleted when a mapper merged its tags onto the building polygon at the same spot, the routine housekeeping the 2026-08-19 adjudication found seven times. way/217484563 answers HTTP 200 and is `amenity=school`, name 'Elliot High Hostel' — our id had been on the wrong polygon all along. Whether the keeper's Overpass query filtered on health tags (making Elliot 'not returned') is NOT reproducible from its capture and is deliberately not asserted here; the disposition is identical either way. All four current ids — way:468966258, way:218396423, way:168965151, way:461683581 — answer 200 with amenity=hospital AND healthcare=hospital. (3) THE '1' AND THE '0' ARE THE SAME READING OF DIFFERENT QUESTIONS. This check's MISSING bucket holds two reasons: 'no element returned' and 'no longer tagged healthcare'. Its 1 is the second reason (cambridge-clinic, the accepted entry below) — its own capture records osm_objects_returned equal to the number checked, i.e. it ALSO measured zero elements gone. (4) #1363'S TWO FACTUAL ERRORS, corrected so they are not re-derived. It states the sweep 'returned an element for all 1,076'; the capture data/capture/osm-tags/2026-08-20.json states records 1076 and elements_found 1073. The gap is NOT three absent facilities — it is three pairs of records sharing one OSM object, every one created by #1228's own repointing (way:468966258, way:218396423, way:461683581). Zero records lack an element. It also states all 1,076 'still carry a healthcare key or a health amenity value'; exactly one does not — way:1103021023, amenity=social_facility, which is the MISSING 1. #1362 repeats that second claim as a premise and should be read with this correction. (5) THE RECONCILIATION EXPOSED A REAL COVERAGE HOLE, fixed the same day. parse_ids keyed a dict by OSM id, so the second record on a shared object silently overwrote the first and was never compared — and because the dropped record left the denominator too, the run printed '1073 records checked' when 1073 was the OBJECT count. A finding was genuinely being lost: ha-grove-hospital-mpumalanga carries 'Ha Grove Hospital' against OSM's 'H.A. Grove Hospital' and never appeared in NAME_CHANGED. The check now compares every record and reports records_checked (1076) and osm_objects_checked (1073) separately. THE ANSWER TO THE ORIGINAL QUESTION IS ZERO: no published facility is gone from OSM. Zero records were edited, zero pages removed, zero URLs changed.

accepted.name: Cambridge Clinic (Sprigg Street Clinic)
accepted.note: OSM IS WRONG AND WE ARE RIGHT — the one disposition of the eight where the source, not the record, is the defect. node:2298902321 was deleted in changeset 181516414 ('Cambridge Clinic') and its tags merged onto the building at the corner of Sprigg and Dominion Street, way:1103021023, which carries our exact phone number (+27 43 726 0142). In merging it the mapper reclassified it as amenity=social_facility / social_facility=day_care / operator:type=private, i.e. a private day-care centre. Second source: Medpages lists 'Sprigg Street Clinic' under Clinics - PUBLIC, Cambridge, East London (orgcode 143929), and directory listings put Cambridge Clinic at Cnr Sprigg St & Dominion St, 5247 — the same corner, the same phone, a public primary-care clinic. The facility_id is repointed at way:1103021023 so the guard keeps watching the object that actually exists; this key accepts the classification disagreement rather than the object's absence. Re-adjudicate if the OSM tags change again — the key includes the reason, so a different tag fires afresh.

$name_adjudication_2026_08_21: The eight NAME_CHANGED findings of the 2026-08-19 capture, adjudicated one at a time under TODO #1281. `name` is declared `sourced` in src/data/_provenance.json, so a name is NEVER swept to match OSM on source equality alone — each of these needed its own second source, and the host of every source was checked first, because a search result corroborating our own data has twice turned out to be our own site. THE HEADLINE RESULT INVERTS THE PREMISE #1281 WAS FILED ON: of its three 'real provincial renames', ONE holds. Ladysmith -> uMnambithi is REFUTED and Fort Beaufort Provincial -> KwaMaqoma is unsupported, and both fail the same way — the TOWN was renamed under the SA Geographical Names Council Act (Ladysmith -> uMnambithi, Fort Beaufort -> KwaMaqoma) and the new town name was propagated onto the FACILITY, which the province never renamed. Treat any OSM facility rename that mirrors a recent South African town rename as suspect by default: that is the reusable lesson here. The two SANTA -> TB renames are real and are corroborated by the Eastern Cape Department of Health's own annual report. One finding was not a rename at all but a name TRANSPOSITION between two adjacent buildings, and one turned up a CLOSED hospital, which is the most important thing this pass found and had nothing to do with names.

name_adjudications.verdict: REFUTED — OSM is wrong, we keep 'Ladysmith Hospital'
name_adjudications.note: The KwaZulu-Natal Department of Health's own facility page, https://www2.kznhealth.gov.za/ladysmithhospital.htm, is titled 'Ladysmith Hospital', was last edited 2025-05-16 (AFTER the town rename), and uses uMnambithi only as the MUNICIPALITY: 'The hospital serves an estimated population of 26 739 (DHIS) that is from the Umnambithi and Indaka Municipality.' The department's CURRENT site lists 'Ladysmith Hospital' at https://www.kznhealth.gov.za/provincial-hospitals/. The hospital's own newsletter for Dec 2024 - May 2025 is masthead-titled 'LADYSMITH REGIONAL HOSPITAL' and contains zero occurrences of 'nambithi'. The 2024/25 Annual Performance Plan uses 'Ladysmith Hospital'. The only places attaching 'uMnambithi' to the hospital are map-derived scrapes with an updated town field. Do NOT publish 'uMnambithi Provincial Hospital'. Side finding, not fixed here: our record's contact.website, http://www.kznhealth.gov.za/ladysmithhospital.htm, now 404s — the page moved to the www2 host.

name_adjudications.verdict: NOT ESTABLISHED — no official source names any hospital KwaMaqoma; we keep ours
name_adjudications.note: The Eastern Cape Department of Health Annual Report 2023/24 — published AFTER the March 2023 town rename — contains ZERO occurrences of 'Maqoma' and calls the facility 'Fort Beaufort Hospital' ('Amathole/BCM 1. Fort Beaufort Hospital Refurbishment', Table B.90 Completed Projects). Wikipedia's Fort Beaufort article confirms the TOWN 'was officially renamed KwaMaqoma in March 2023' while naming the facility 'Fort Beaufort Provincial Hospital'. The single web hit for the string 'KwaMaqoma Provincial Hospital' is a Google-Places scrape which also places the facility in the wrong town; discarded. Same failure mode as Ladysmith. Separately, and NOT changed here because it is a different question from the one #1281 asked: our name 'Fort Beaufort Provincial' is missing the word 'Hospital', and the province's own string is 'Fort Beaufort Hospital'.

name_adjudications.verdict: RENAME CONFIRMED — applied, with the old name kept as a suffix
name_adjudications.note: The Eastern Cape Department of Health Annual Report 2023/24 lists 'Winterberg' among the province's ten specialised TB hospitals and carries 'Winterberg TB Hospital - Refurbishment' in Table B.90; the department's document library holds a vacancy notice for 'CEO Winterberg TB Hospital'. Wikipedia's Fort Beaufort article makes the link explicit: 'Winterberg TB (previous SANTA) Hospital'. A legacy directory carrying ecdoh.gov.za record links has 'Winterberg SANTA Hospital', Fort Beaufort, telephone +27 (46) 645 1142. The OSM object itself supports the identity rather than merely asserting the name: VisibleSouth (an experienced South African mapper, ~6,400 changesets) set old_name='Winterberg Santa Hospital' on this way in a changeset commented 'Winterberg TB Hospital'. Published as 'Winterberg TB Hospital (formerly SANTA Hospital)' — the current name is what a searcher types now, and the suffix keeps the old query matching, exactly as the Gizenga Mpanza record does for Stanger. OPEN CAVEAT, deliberately not resolved by guessing: the facility-to-COORDINATE identity is not independently verified — secondary sources place Winterberg on Alice Road about 5 km from Fort Beaufort, and echealth.gov.za was unreachable throughout. That is a pre-existing question about this record's position, unchanged by the rename.

name_adjudications.verdict: RENAME CONFIRMED but MOOT — the hospital is CLOSED; handled in care-role.ts instead
name_adjudications.note: The rename is real ('Temba TB Hospital' is the department's own string) but it is not the finding that matters. Temba TB Hospital closed on 2023-07-01: the Eastern Cape Department of Health's Annual Report 2023/24 says 'The hospital has been moved from Temba hospital premises which was being rented under Grahamstown TB Association and has been relocated to Settler's hospital'; Spotlight (2023-09-13) reports 'On 1 July this year, Makhanda's only TB hospital, Temba TB Hospital, also shut its doors'; Grocott's Mail (2023-07-13) found 'the buildings were deserted' on 12 July and reported the 31 staff moving to Settlers Hospital, with a 2024 follow-up on the building being vandalised. We were publishing an abandoned building as an operating district hospital, with a telephone number. The NAME is deliberately left as 'Temba SANTA Hospital': nobody needs to find a closed hospital in order to get care, they need to be told it closed and where to go, and our name is the one local searchers still use. The page now carries a care-role entry naming Settlers Hospital, Milner Street, Makhanda. Contrast with the Winterberg decision above — that facility is OPERATING under a new name, so there the current name is what a searcher needs.

name_adjudications.verdict: NOT A RENAME AND NOT A CARE-ROLE CASE — OSM transposed two names; we keep ours, UNSETTLED
name_adjudications.note: #1281 read this as 'if true, not a care facility at all'. The premise does not survive the object history. daxro (4,025 changesets, comment 'Add local POIs') created BOTH adjacent buildings in changeset 164356915 on 2025-04-01, consistently: way 1373584712 'Palm Ridge Community Hall' with amenity=community_centre + community_centre=community_hall, and way 1373584714 (ours) 'Palm Ridge Clinic' with amenity=clinic + healthcare=clinic, about 140 m apart beside Palm Ridge Primary School. In changeset 185746119 on 2026-07-14 — no changeset comment, by an account with three changesets in total — ONLY THE TWO NAMES WERE SWAPPED, leaving both tag sets untouched. Both objects are now internally self-contradictory: ours reads clinic tags under the hall's name, and its neighbour reads community-hall tags under the clinic's name. OSM therefore does not assert that our building is a community hall; it asserts a transposition. Which of the two readings is right — crossed names, or a local correction of the names with the tags left stale — is NOT settled, and the honest reason it does not matter much is that both readings put a real Palm Ridge Clinic within 140 m, nothing like the 1.3-1.9 km errors #1228 found. No change made. Do NOT add this to care-role.ts on the strength of the OSM name.

name_adjudications.verdict: KEEP OURS — OSM replaced the name with its acronym
name_adjudications.note: The same OSM object corroborates our name from its own tags: operator='Aids Training, Information and Counselling Centre'. Our expanded form is strictly the more findable of the two and contains the acronym's expansion verbatim, so nothing is lost. No second source needed — this is not a claim about the world changing, it is OSM choosing a shorter string.

name_adjudications.verdict: KEEP OURS — OSM dropped the '(formerly Stanger Hospital)' suffix and we keep it deliberately
name_adjudications.note: Not a rename in either direction: the current name is identical, and OSM merely dropped the parenthetical. People still search 'Stanger Hospital', so the suffix is doing findability work, and it is the in-repo precedent for how a renamed facility keeps its old query — the Winterberg record above now follows it.

name_adjudications.verdict: NOT SETTLED — a fuller form of the same name, not a new one; left as ours
name_adjudications.note: This is the record #1228 repointed at way 461683581, the polygon that carries the hospital's own tags at 1 Maclear Road, Khowa. 'Elliot Provincial Hospital' is a fuller rendering of the same name rather than a rename, and no second source was consulted for it, so nothing is changed. Note that our own corpus holds a SECOND, withheld record literally named 'Elliot Provincial Hospital' (withheld as a duplicate-osm-object by #1228), so adopting that string here would make two of our records identical in name as well as in id — a reason for caution, not evidence either way. Low stakes: neither string misleads a searcher.

name_adjudications.verdict: KEEP OURS — a punctuation variant, and the drifted record is not published
name_adjudications.note: Surfaced by the #1351/#1363 fix, not by the 2026-08-19 capture: this finding had been silently dropped because two records share OSM object way:468966258 and the second overwrote the first in the comparison dict. No second source is needed, because nothing here is a claim about the world changing. 'Ha Grove Hospital' and 'H.A. Grove Hospital' are the same name with different punctuation, and the record OSM disagrees with, ha-grove-hospital-mpumalanga, is WITHHELD as duplicate-osm-object — noindexed and absent from the sitemap since #1228. The record we actually publish for this hospital, ha-grove-hospital-belfast-mpumalanga, already carries OSM's exact string 'H.A. Grove Hospital'. No searcher is affected either way, so editing a sourced name here would be churn.
